transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-03-03 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Patel (Solaris - Head of ML), Priya Rao (Eng Lead), Evan Morris (Data Eng), Sophie Li (Security), Speaker 6

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Solaris is evaluating embeddings + reranking for search relevance on their customer support and docs product. Primary considerations: throughput/QPS and cost, vector DB choice (they currently run FAISS in-house), embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), hybrid search (BM25 + vectors), and security/privacy (VPC, KMS, SOC2). They asked about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Next steps: share pricing, benchmark template, and kickoff POC.

Topics: embeddings model selection, dimensionality tradeoffs, vector DB integration, throughput and batching, hybrid search architecture, security and compliance, POC scoping.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Rafael, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam: Good thanks, sorry for the slight delay we had a standup run over. Liam here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, all set.
[00:12] Evan: Evan, ready.
[00:14] Sophie: Sophie from security.
[00:15] Rafael: Hi team. Quick agenda: 1) understand your current stack and success criteria, 2) talk embeddings + rerank options, 3) discuss hosting modes and security, 4) next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:22] Liam: Yep that works. I'll start with the problem space: our product surface is a docs + support search, customers are complaining about relevance when queries are short or ambiguous. We currently run a FAISS-based vector index on prem with sentence-transformers 768-dim embeddings, and a BM25 hybrid layer. It's okay but cost of running GPUs for embedding generation and the latency for rerank is an issue. We also want a simpler path to evaluate better embeddings and possibly offload serving.
[00:45] Rafael: Got it. Can you share rough numbers for QPS, vector count, and latency SLOs?
[00:50] Liam: So core traffic is 2k QPS peak across our region, but search queries are about 200 QPS sustained; rerank is invoked on the top 50 candidates, so end-to-end target is under 200ms P95 for search+rerank ideally. Document corpus ~10M docs, average embedding vector dim 768 today.
[01:18] Priya: Also want to mention cost sensitivity—if embeddings double dimensionality and costs go up 2x we need to justify it.
[01:26] Rafael: Totally. There's a few levers: embedding dimensionality affects index size and vector DB throughput, but better embeddings sometimes let you reduce rerank candidates. We often recommend testing 768 vs 1536 or 1024 depending on model family. For hosted Redwood embeddings we support multiple dimensions; for customers who want to run in Dedicated or Private you can bring your model or use our catalog.
[01:49] Liam: For vector DBs, we're tied into FAISS and an in-house cold store. We're exploring Pinecone or Milvus for managed service. How does Redwood integrate?
[01:58] Maya: Redwood integrates with external vector DBs via standard APIs — we can stream embeddings into Pinecone, Milvus, or Weaviate, or you can keep FAISS and use Redwood for embedding generation + rerank hosting. For Dedicated we can colocate with your vector DB, and for Private you get full VPC control.
[02:15] Evan: If we keep FAISS, we worry about throughput — our ingestion pipeline spikes during ingestion and reindexing. Does Redwood provide batching or streaming helpers?
[02:24] Rafael: Yes, we provide ingestion tooling and a benchmark template. For Hosted, we have a managed ingestion pipeline and recommended batching sizes; for Dedicated/Private you can run the same pipeline with our SDKs. We also suggest prefix caching for common queries to reduce repeated compute.
[02:40] Sophie: Security question: we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, audit logs, and KMS-managed encryption of keys. Also data residency in EU for a subset. Can Redwood meet those?
[02:51] Maya: Short answer: yes. Hosted is SOC2, SAML/SSO, and we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. Private can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem for strict residency. We'll share the security pack but we need to confirm specific EU region availability for hosted.
[03:06] Sophie: Okay we'll need the SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc.
[03:09] Maya: We'll send that after the call.
[03:11] Rafael: A few technical clarifications on rerank: are you running a two-stage retrieval (BM25 -> vector -> rerank) or a single pass?
[03:18] Liam: It's BM25 to get seed candidates, then FAISS vectors to re-score, then a small cross-encoder neural reranker we host on CPU that runs on the top 20.
[03:28] Rafael: Good — common pattern. With Redwood's rerank service you can run the cross-encoder on GPU for lower latency, or use optimized hybrid search to reduce candidate set. For 200 QPS and top-50 rerank, GPU-backed dedicated instances usually make sense; for proof-of-concept you can try Hosted but you might hit higher per-token costs.
[03:45] Priya: When you say top-50, is that fast enough to meet our 200ms P95?
[03:50] Rafael: It depends on the model size and batching. If your cross-encoder is small (distil or tiny transformer) and you batch across requests with micro-batching, you can hit sub-200ms P95 on Dedicated. For Hosted we'll need to benchmark — I'll share our latency spreadsheet.
[04:07] Liam: We also want to support hybrid search where BM25 features are combined with vector cosine sim and learned weights. Any guidance on feature stitching?
[04:16] Rafael: We usually recommend scoring pipelines where BM25 score is normalized and concatenated with vector similarity and passed to a small ranker. Redwood supports streaming scores into our reranker and structured output for the final ranking. For hybrid, we can help tune features and suggest how many candidates to keep.
[04:32] Speaker 6: Quick question, what's the cost difference roughly for embeddings at 1536 dim vs 768 in Redwood Hosted?
[04:38] Maya: Ballpark — embeddings cost scales with dimension and tokens; 1536 might be ~1.8-2x cost of 768 in hosted. But if higher-dim embeddings reduce downstream rerank cost or candidate size, net cost could be neutral. We'll provide a breakdown.
[04:55] Evan: On vector DB side, moving from 768->1536 doubles index size which affects memory and cost on Pinecone/Milvus. So we need to evaluate tradeoffs end-to-end.
[05:05] Rafael: Exactly. That's why the POC should include 1) sample of top queries, 2) A/B with 768 vs 1536, 3) measure recall@k and rerank cost, 4) end-to-end latency. We'll provide a template.
[05:20] Liam: Ok that makes sense. On the Private/dedicated options — what are the latencies we'd expect if we put Redwood Dedicated in our cloud region vs Hosted in Redwood's region?
[05:30] Rafael: If you colocate Dedicated in your region, network RTTs are minimal and you'll typically see lower latency. Hosted can be regionally proxied but if the Hosted region is different you'll add ~20-50ms. For strict P95 SLOs, Dedicated or Private in-region is safer.
[05:44] Priya: For the POC, roughly how much setup for Dedicated? We don't want a 4-week onramp.
[05:51] Maya: Dedicated can be provisioned in a couple of weeks with standard configs; Private on-prem is longer. For quick evaluation we recommend Hosted POC + a small Dedicated trial if you want to validate latency.
[06:05] Sophie: One more security nuance — we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest, and isolated logging. Do you offer token-level redaction?
[06:14] Rafael: Yes, we support TLS, KMS for at-rest, and redaction controls. For Dedicated/Private you can ship logs to your SIEM and we support RBAC and token-level controls. We'll include the security docs.
[06:26] Liam: Let's talk about throughput: 200 QPS with top-50 rerank, what's a recommended instance shape?
[06:33] Rafael: For GPU inference with cross-encoders, a few N GPU config options: A single A100-equivalent for high throughput, or multiple T4s for cost balance. We usually run benchmarks — for a 12-layer cross-encoder you might need 1 A100 to get ~200-300 QPS with batching; smaller models can do more. Rafael: (note: these numbers are approximate, we'll run exact bench).
[06:57] Priya: Are there recommended quantization options to reduce cost?
[07:01] Rafael: Yes, we support int8 and mixed-precision paths; quantization can reduce memory and increase throughput but may slightly affect quality. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per model and workload.
[07:12] Liam: On model selection for embeddings — do you have specific model families you recommend for docs search?
[07:18] Rafael: We have a model catalog; for semantic search we often recommend models in the OpenAI-text-sim family or similar open models — for example a 1536-d embedding model often gives stronger separation, but many customers see excellent results with modern 768-d models. We can run quick evals on your test set.
[07:33] Evan: For ingestion, what's the recommended pipeline for upserts and reindexing with minimal downtime?
[07:39] Rafael: We recommend incremental upserts with versioned documents and background reindexing. For large reindexes we use snapshot + swap to avoid downtime. We'll share our ingestion cookbook.
[07:51] Priya: About cost — if we do Dedicated there's a reserved capacity commit, can you explain the pricing model?
[07:58] Maya: Dedicated is committed monthly/annual capacity with discounted unit price; Hosted is pay-as-you-go. There's also Private licensing models. We'll include a pricing sheet with examples tied to QPS and model choices.
[08:11] Liam: Any limits on embedding throughput in Hosted? We have bursts during marketing campaigns.
[08:16] Maya: Hosted has rate limits but we can discuss burst policies; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can configure autoscaling/burst.
[08:24] Sophie: For compliance we need an SLA. Does Redwood offer SLA on Hosted?
[08:29] Maya: Hosted has published uptime SLAs for paid tiers; Dedicated has stronger SLA options. We'll include SLA language in the follow-up.
[08:37] Speaker 6: How long of a POC do you recommend?
[08:40] Rafael: Typically 2-4 weeks for an embeddings + rerank POC: first week ingest sample data and baseline, second week run A/B experiments and tune, third week finalize metrics and cost analysis. If you want to validate Dedicated latency, add a short Dedicated trial.
[08:55] Liam: Sounds good. Let's lock down next steps.
[08:58] Maya: Recap: 1) we'll send pricing sheet, security pack (SOC2, KMS docs), and benchmark template; 2) Rafa will share ingestion cookbook and latency spreadsheet; 3) Solaris to send sample queries, sample docs, and QPS distribution by 2026-03-10; 4) schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-03-16.
[09:18] Priya: We'll also confirm which vector DB we want to test — likely Pinecone and our FAISS baseline.
[09:24] Evan: I'll package a dataset export.
[09:27] Sophie: We'll review the security docs once received.
[09:29] Maya: Great, I'll follow up with links to the shared deck and benchmark spreadsheet. Deck link: https://redwood.app/decks/solar-kickoff (placeholder)
[09:36] Liam: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[09:38] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
